topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing for the lecture, outlining the speaker's background, course structure, and learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological Nature and Multi-Factorial Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental nature of cancer as a genetic and evolutionary disease shaped by intrinsic cellular errors, inherited predispositions, and microenvironmental conditions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence of Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine environmental carcinogen exposures and evaluate epidemiological evidence comparing environmental influences to random chance in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological pathogens drive cancer, illustrating the concept through the detailed etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Radiation Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which specific dietary toxins, UV radiation, and metabolized chemical carcinogens induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic promotional mechanisms of carcinogenesis, including chronic inflammation, cell signalling activation, and host developmental susceptibility windows.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect and establish the carcinogenicity of specific agents.

topics.label: Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure within everyday risk-benefit decisions and summarising the main takeaways.
